Combined, the underlying defect is always-repro'd: confirmed with -Vd (validation disabled) that main-debug still internally produces the same illegal i33 zext/mul/lshr/trunc sequence. summary: The reported defect (SCEV widens the loop's overflow-guarded closed-form multiply ((input-1)*(input-2))/2 to an illegal i33 DXIL integer type) is unfixed and reproduces on every catalogued release and on main-debug. What changed, precisely between v1.9.2602.24 and v1.9.2607, is that the DXIL validator's Types.IntWidth rule now rejects the module (error: Int type 'i33' has an invalid width., exit 0x80004005) instead of letting it through silently as it did on all 20 older releases. Confirmed with -Vd that the illegal type is still produced internally on main-debug even though validation now blocks it. The reporter's literal as-filed command (-T lib_6_3, no -E) is a separate dead end on current main: without a [shader] attribute CSMain is not recognized as a library entry point, so it compiles an empty library; the maintainer's own corrected repro (-T cs_6_3 -ECSMain, confirmed via the thread's self-corrected close/reopen within two minutes on 2024-09-25) is what still demonstrates the defect today. Two negative controls (no loop; same loop shape without a closed-form summation) both score no-repro under both predicates, confirming discrimination.
text_stale: The title and body describe the compile succeeding with an illegal i33 type silently visible in the disassembly. That silent shape stopped occurring at v1.9.2607: on current main-debug the exact same input now hard-fails to compile with error: Int type 'i33' has an invalid width. (exit 0x80004005), so a naive spot-check of the literal reported wording now reads as cannot-reproduce for a defect that is, in fact, still fully present (confirmed internally via -Vd). A reader should not close this as fixed.
title: HLSL loop optimization results in an unsupported i33 type
